On 11 November 1965 the white minority government of Southern Rhodesia, led by Prime Minister Ian Smith, declared independence from Britain rather than accept a path to majority rule.

Britain refused to use force but called the act illegal, and the United Nations imposed sanctions, the first mandatory sanctions in its history. No country recognised Rhodesia, but South Africa and Portuguese Mozambique helped it trade, and its economy at first grew.

Smith said there would be no majority rule in a thousand years. African nationalists, their parties banned and leaders jailed, turned to armed struggle in the Bush War. It ended with the Lancaster House Agreement of 1979.
sum: On 11 November 1965 the white minority government of Southern Rhodesia, led by Prime Minister Ian Smith, declared independence from Britain rather than accept a path to majority rule.
